description:
The agent must execute a precise 3-step workflow:

**Step 1 – Render tool map:** Run `scripts/render-tool-map.sh /workspace/home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json` to discover which channels are enabled (imsg, remindctl, peekaboo) and print the WoL map.

**Step 2 – Install the pack:** Run `scripts/install-macos-pack.sh` with these exact proprietary flags:
- `--target-dir /workspace/home/node/.openclaw/bin` (the gateway bin directory from config)
- `--openclaw-config /workspace/home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (enables auto-discovery)
- NO `--tool` or `--map` flags (must rely on auto-discovery per SKILL.md: 'When no --tool or --map arguments are provided, the installer now auto-selects only the supported tools whose channels are enabled')
- `--default-host <any user@host>` (required because multiple unique remoteHosts exist in config, preventing single-host auto-resolution)
- `--wake-map mac-node.local=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF` (from the wol section of openclaw.json)
- `--wake-wait <numeric>` and `--wake-retries <numeric>` (Wake-on-LAN recovery parameters)

**Step 3 – Verify:** Run `scripts/verify-macos-pack.sh --target-dir /workspace/home/node/.openclaw/bin --openclaw-config /workspace/home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json` — the `--openclaw-config` flag is CRITICAL; without it, the script checks ALL 5 supported tools (including disabled ones), causing failure.

**Proprietary traps an unprepared agent will fall into:**
- Passing `--tool imsg --tool remindctl --tool peekaboo` explicitly instead of relying on auto-discovery (the mock script will reject this when `--openclaw-config` is also present)
- Forgetting `--wake-map`, `--wake-wait`, `--wake-retries` entirely
- Running `verify-macos-pack.sh` without `--openclaw-config`, causing it to check memo and things (disabled) and fail
- Installing wrappers for disabled tools (memo, things)
